title: Federal Reserve G.17 annual revision of industrial production and capacity utilization — 2022 base year, 2023 and 2024 Census benchmarks, seven days after the October print
source: FED: two federalreserve.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-11-09 (both HTTP 200). (1) The Board's G.17 announcements feed (feeds/g17.html, 619,956 bytes), posting dated September 18, 2026 and titled 'G.17 Annual Revision Planned to be Released on November 24, 2026': 'The Federal Reserve Board plans to issue its annual revision to the indexes of industrial production (IP) and the related measures of capacity utilization on November 24, 2026. The base year for the revised indexes will be 2022. New annual benchmark data for manufacturing from the U.S. Census Bureau for 2023 and 2024 will be incorporated'. (2) The same notice, still carried under the 'Revision of Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization Notice' banner of the current G.17 release page (releases/g17/current/default.htm, 116,335 bytes, release date October 16, 2026), unchanged 52 days on. PROMOTED from the estimate the industrial-production-2026-11-17 pulse filed, which could not self-confirm its own in-sweep discovery. The Board's verb is 'plans to issue', not 'tentatively plans' (the wording of its 2025-04-16 placeholder notice, which named only a quarter): in the feed's own record every date-specific annual-revision notice found, eight of eight (2017-03-31, 2018-03-23, 2019-03-27, 2021-05-28, 2022-06-28, 2023-03-28, 2024-06-28, 2025-11-24), was followed by the revision on exactly the date it named, including 2025's, announced 2025-11-12 just after a funding lapse that had pushed two monthly G.17 releases to December. No release time is stated. Checked 2026-11-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-11-09 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/industrial-production-annual-revision-2026-11-24.from-industrial-production-2026-11-17.json, now shadowed and inert). Every claim in that proposal was re-fetched from the Board rather than carried; all survive. The status moved estimate to confirmed on the strength of the eight-of-eight record in the source string, not on a time announcement (the proposer suggested a time as the bar; none has been posted, and the ledger says so). WHY IT IS A CALENDAR ENTRY AND NOT JUST A NOTE: it is the restatement event for the series, a standalone release in every precedent in the Board's feed (noon EST in 2025). The October level printed 2026-11-17 and every percentile in the 11-17 ledger are restated a week later. Impact LOW and symbols [] match its parent: no house playbook is macro-keyed and no instrument attaches. What gets revised: base year 2017 to 2022; 2023 and 2024 Census manufacturing benchmarks; seasonal factors for each industry; capacity through Q4 2025 (Census Quarterly Survey of Plant Capacity Utilization) plus USGS and DOE capacity data. Size record from the Board's own release summaries: 2022 little revision to manufacturing growth, higher utilization; 2023 total IP growth rates revised by no more than 0.6pp in any year, utilization little changed; 2024 (no new benchmark) years unchanged, 2020 up and 2023 down 0.1pp; 2025 manufacturing output revised from a rise to a decline of more than 1-1/2% net from Feb 2020 through Aug 2025, Aug 2025 manufacturing utilization 1-1/4ppt below its previous estimate.
